cards.title: Creative Is the New Meta Targeting Under Andromeda
cards.summary: Meta's Andromeda algorithm scans creative assets themselves to find buyers, making manual interest and lookalike targeting largely obsolete.
cards.use_when: Planning a Meta ad account structure and deciding how much effort to put into interest/lookalike targeting versus creative production.
steps: Treat the ad creative itself as your primary targeting input: the system reads ad transcripts, copy, and visuals to identify and match buyers, so the creative's theme, language, and imagery determine who sees it.
Stop building campaigns around granular interest stacks or lookalike layers as the main lever, since the algorithm's vector-based targeting supersedes them.
Instead, encode your target persona and angle directly into the creative concept so the algorithm has explicit signals for who should receive the ad.
Audit your existing adsets to confirm each one carries a clear, consistent audience signal rather than relying on a manually configured interest selection.
Reallocate planning time from audience-list building toward producing more distinct creative concepts, since creative now drives audience selection and reach.
caveats: This reflects the source's description of Meta's Andromeda behavior; verify current platform mechanics as they change.
cards.source_name: The Creative Strategy Behind $100M_yr of Meta Spend.docx

cards.title: Creative Similarity Score and Its Reach Penalty
cards.summary: Andromeda bundles visually or thematically similar creatives under one entity ID, forcing them to compete for the same audience and inflating frequency while depressing ROAS.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing rising frequency, flat or falling ROAS, and shrinking unique reach across a Meta ad account.
steps: Recognize that when creatives look or feel similar, Andromeda groups them under a single entity ID and serves them to the same audience cluster.
Treat clustered creatives as a red flag: they restrict unique reach, drive frequency up, and degrade ROAS as the same people see near-identical ads.
When you see frequency climbing and unique reach stalling, assume creative similarity is the cause before blaming audiences or budget.
Deliberately diversify visual style, concept, angle, and format across ads to reduce similarity, rather than producing iterative variations of one winner.
Periodically review your ad library as a whole and ask whether a machine could easily tell your ads apart; if not, force more conceptual distance between them.
caveats: The 'Creative Similarity Score' is the source's characterization of Meta's behavior, not a metric you can directly read in Ads Manager.
cards.source_name: The Creative Strategy Behind $100M_yr of Meta Spend.docx

cards.title: Architect Adsets by Concept, Not by Arbitrary Traits
cards.summary: Consolidate creative variations into concept-specific adsets built on Persona plus Angle plus Offer to feed the algorithm clean learning signals.
cards.use_when: Setting up or restructuring Meta ad account adsets before scaling spend.
steps: Define each adset around a single coherent concept expressed as Persona + Angle + Offer, so the algorithm receives one clear signal per adset.
Do not segment adsets by arbitrary traits such as launch dates, which fragment learning without meaning.
Do not mix conflicting personas (for example men and women) inside the same adset, since conflicting signals confuse the machine learning targeting models.
Group all creative variations that share the same persona, angle, and offer into one adset rather than splitting them by minor visual differences.
Review your account's adsets for any that combine inconsistent audiences or offers and consolidate or split them so each adset carries one signal.
caveats: Some deliberate multi-persona testing structures exist; the source's rule specifically warns against mixing conflicting personas within a single adset.
cards.source_name: The Creative Strategy Behind $100M_yr of Meta Spend.docx

cards.title: Amount Spent as the Creative Performance Proxy
cards.summary: Because Meta optimizes for multi-click and view-through journeys, amount spent is a more reliable ad-level proxy for creative performance than last-click ROAS.
cards.use_when: Evaluating which top-of-funnel Meta creatives to keep, cut, or scale.
steps: Recognize that Meta optimizes ad delivery for multi-click and view-through journeys, so in-platform ad-level last-click ROAS is highly unreliable for top-of-funnel creative.
Use Amount Spent as the most reliable proxy metric for creative performance at the ad level, since Meta allocates budget toward ads it believes perform in the multi-touch sequence.
Do not kill a top-of-funnel creative solely because its ad-level last-click ROAS looks weak; correlate performance at the adset or account level instead.
Combine amount spent with your own incrementality or blended measurement to validate creative impact, rather than trusting platform-reported last-click numbers.
Apply this especially when judging prospecting creative that by design will not show strong direct last-click returns.
caveats: This distinguishes ad-level last-click ROAS from blended or incrementality-based measurement; do not read it as saying ROAS is meaningless in aggregate.
cards.source_name: The Creative Strategy Behind $100M_yr of Meta Spend.docx

cards.title: Track KPIs at Adset Level to Avoid Last-Click Flaws
cards.summary: Adset-level KPI tracking is more reliable than ad-level for creative decisions because the algorithm optimizes multi-touch paths.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to structure reporting and which creative to cut during active Meta campaigns.
steps: Set your primary creative-evaluation reporting at the adset level rather than the individual ad level.
Understand that ad-level metrics are distorted by Meta's multi-touch and view-through optimization, which credits and routes budget across a sequence rather than a single click.
Use adset-level performance to make keep-cut-scale decisions, comparing concept-level (Persona + Angle + Offer) results rather than individual ad ROAS.
Use ad-level Amount Spent as a directional signal of which creative the algorithm is favoring, not as a profit verdict.
Pair platform adset metrics with a blended or third-party measurement layer to confirm true incremental value.
caveats: Adset-level tracking still inherits platform attribution limitations; it reduces noise rather than eliminating it.
cards.source_name: The Creative Strategy Behind $100M_yr of Meta Spend.docx

cards.title: Avoid the DPA Death Spiral Masking Weak Prospecting
cards.summary: Dynamic Product Ads can inflate bottom-of-funnel retargeting ROAS while hiding poor top-of-funnel performance.
cards.use_when: Reviewing retargeting or catalog campaigns when overall performance looks strong but new-customer growth is weak.
steps: Recognize that DPAs (Dynamic Product Ads) frequently deliver high retargeting ROAS by re-engaging people already close to purchase.
Watch for the 'death spiral': strong DPA retargeting numbers masking poor top-of-funnel prospecting performance.
Separate prospecting and retargeting reporting so DPA-driven bottom-of-funnel ROAS cannot cover for weak top-of-funnel results.
Evaluate DPAs on new-customer or incremental metrics, not just blended ROAS, to see whether they are truly adding revenue or just harvesting existing demand.
If top-of-funnel acquisition is weak, fix creative and prospecting rather than leaning harder on DPAs for headline ROAS.
caveats: DPAs are not inherently bad; the risk is using them to mask weak prospecting in blended reporting.
cards.source_name: The Creative Strategy Behind $100M_yr of Meta Spend.docx

cards.title: Portfolio Scaling to Avoid Hero-Ad Dependence
cards.summary: Rely on a portfolio of recognizable creative concepts rather than a single hero ad that will hit its spend ceiling and fatigue.
cards.use_when: Scaling Meta spend and deciding whether to concentrate budget on one winner or distribute across a roster.
steps: Reject the single 'hero ad' strategy: any one ad eventually reaches its maximum daily spend capacity and fatigues.
Build a portfolio of distinct creative concepts so spend can shift as individual ads plateau.
Track which concepts are absorbing budget and continuously introduce new ones to replace fatiguing winners.
Maintain production volume high enough that new creative is always available to feed the portfolio, since scaling depends on supply of fresh concepts.
When an ad nears its ceiling, shift incremental budget to other proven concepts rather than only forcing spend into the fatiguing one.
caveats: Portfolio approaches require more creative production capacity and budget than a single-winner strategy.
cards.source_name: The Creative Strategy Behind $100M_yr of Meta Spend.docx

cards.title: CBO and the 4/64 Pareto Spend Pattern
cards.summary: Campaign Budget Optimization exploits Pareto concentration where roughly 4% of ads command about 64% of spend, but over-concentration creates revenue risk.
cards.use_when: Setting budget distribution rules for Meta campaigns and deciding how much to let the algorithm concentrate spend.
steps: Use Campaign Budget Optimization (CBO) to let the algorithm route budget toward the best-performing ads efficiently.
Expect strong concentration: per the source's Pareto observation, roughly 4% of ads command about 64% of spend, so a small set of ads will carry most delivery.
Monitor for over-concentration, since depending on a tiny number of ads exposes the business to sudden revenue drops if those ads fatigue or break.
Keep a pipeline of back-up concepts ready so that when the top ads decline, replacements already have delivery history.
Balance CBO efficiency against risk by setting guardrails that ensure not all budget is hostage to a few ads.
caveats: The 4%/64% figure is the source's heuristic observation of spend distribution, not a guaranteed ratio.
cards.source_name: The Creative Strategy Behind $100M_yr of Meta Spend.docx

cards.title: Allocate 10-25% of Media Budget to Creative Production
cards.summary: Reserve a meaningful share of media spend for creative production, scaled to the brand's spend level, to sustain the volume needed to combat fatigue.
cards.use_when: Setting the creative production budget for a Meta advertising program.
steps: Commit a minimum allocation of 10% to 25% of total media budget directly to creative production.
Scale the percentage to spend level: per the source, allocate around 25% of media spend for brands spending $30K-$100K per month.
For brands spending over $100K per month, the source suggests scaling the creative allocation down toward 10%.
Treat the creative budget as a volume requirement, not a nice-to-have: sustained ad volume is what keeps fatigue from eroding performance.
Review creative output against this budget regularly to confirm production volume is actually matching the pace of fatigue.
caveats: The 25% and 10% figures are the source's recommended benchmarks tied to specific spend bands, not universal rules; adjust for your production model.
cards.source_name: The Creative Strategy Behind $100M_yr of Meta Spend.docx

cards.title: Sequence Ads for Multi-Click and View-Through Journeys
cards.summary: Meta optimizes for multi-touch journeys, so plan ad sequencing and evaluate performance across the journey rather than on isolated clicks.
cards.use_when: Planning ad sequencing and measuring a multi-stage Meta funnel from prospecting to conversion.
steps: Recognize that Meta's algorithm optimizes for multi-click and view-through journeys, not single-click attribution.
Plan ad sequencing so prospects see coherent messaging across exposures rather than unrelated one-off ads.
Interpret performance across the journey: an ad that generates views and later clicks may look weak at the ad level but perform in sequence.
Do not over-optimize early-funnel ads for last-click results, since that misaligns with how the algorithm sequences delivery.
Use journey-aware reporting (blended or incrementality measures) to judge whether the sequence as a whole is driving conversion.
caveats: View-through and multi-click attribution can overstate causal impact if used alone; pair with incrementality testing.
cards.source_name: The Creative Strategy Behind $100M_yr of Meta Spend.docx
